source.title: CM values of higher automorphic Green functions for orthogonal groups
source.authors: Jan Hendrik Bruinier, Stephan Ehlen and Tonghai Yang
extractionReadingHistory: Published version (open access, CC BY 4.0), read in full on 2026-09-22 (PDF SHA-256 729e4f9daff82e8e98ae27bcd8084c4e89c8a08b91f2b5106c048ab35cda4160). Statement numbers and pages are the published ones; the appendix is Section 9 there.

Checked in detail: Lemma 3.1, Proposition 3.6, the proofs of Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 5.4, Corollary 5.9, Proposition 6.2, the Gamma factors of Lemma 6.3 and Theorem 6.5, Proposition 6.7 and Lemma 6.8 (symbolically, j ≤ 5), Proposition 6.16, the constants in Theorem 7.9, (7.10), Theorem 7.11 and Example 3, the counting in Corollary 7.18, and Proposition 9.6. The cited results of Bruinier (LNM 1780), Oda–Tsuzuki, Kudla–Yang, Bruinier–Yang, Zhang, Xue, Howard, Duke–Jenkins, Alfes-Neumann–Schwagenscheidt and Howard–Madapusi Pera were used as quoted.

Checked all 46 input rows against those statements and surrounding hypotheses. Journal-page locators and every source finding were checked in the 93-page published PDF; selected formula pages were additionally inspected as images. This is not a claim to a new complete word-level PDF/TeX diff or to reading all prerequisite originals. Historical extraction reading claims are preserved separately.

summary: The paper develops higher regularized theta lifts on orthogonal Shimura varieties, small and big CM-value formulas, arithmetic preimages of binary theta series, partial averages via Zagier/Millson lifts, and a higher-weight Gross–Kohnen–Zagier theorem. The extraction requires revision. The original 46 rows bundle many separate definitions and results; proof suppliers, API contracts and tests are not recursively closed. This review corrects clear hypotheses and locators, credits existing shifted Legendre polynomials and quadratic two-rank theory, and records 27 confirmed source findings with carefully bounded conclusions. In particular the earlier proposed odd-j constant repair is not established: p_z sign, Poincare-series normalization and SL/PSL multiplicities must be reconciled together. Example 3 also confuses two nonisometric discriminant-63 lattices. Every missing aggregate is provisionally routed once, but no route is accepted for intake in this review.

items.name: Definition 7.1 and Lemmas 7.2–7.3: local genus characters χ_Δ
items.statement: For a fundamental discriminant Δ and λ = [[b/2, −a], [c, −b/2]] ∈ L′_p with 4Q(λ) ∈ ΔZ_p, χ_{Δ,p}(λ) = (n, Δ)_p if gcd(a, b, c, Δ) = 1 and [a, b, c] represents n with (Δ, n) = 1, and 0 otherwise; χ_Δ = ∏_p χ_{Δ,p}. Lemma 7.2: χ_{Δ,p} is well defined and for p | Δ equals (a, Δ)_p if p ∤ a, (c, Δ)_p if p ∤ c, and 0 otherwise; on L it is the classical genus character (Gross–Kohnen–Zagier I.2). Lemma 7.3: χ_{Δ,p}(h·λ) = (det h, Δ)_p χ_{Δ,p}(λ) for h ∈ GL_2(Z_p).

items.name: Genus theory: class groups of exponent 2
items.statement: For a negative fundamental discriminant D′ with s prime divisors, the genus characters χ_Δ (D′ = Δ·Δ̃ with Δ, Δ̃ fundamental) are the characters of Cl(O_{D′})/Cl(O_{D′})²; if Cl(O_{D′}) has exponent ≤ 2 then h(D′) = 2^{s−1}, every class-group character is a genus character, and H_{D′} = k_{D′}(√Δ_1, …, √Δ_{2^{s−1}}).

items.name: Conjecture 1.1 (Gross–Zagier) and the higher Green functions G_{j+1,f}
items.statement: Conjecture 1.1 is a conjecture, not a theorem to import. Define the raw series only for Re(s)>1 and off the relevant Hecke divisors. Its printed SL_2 normalization is inconsistent with the later PSL_2 local-singularity coefficient (E25); the convention is an unresolved comparison obligation. G_s(z_1, z_2) = −2Σ_{γ∈SL_2(Z)}Q_{s−1}(1 + |z_1 − γz_2|²/(2Im z_1 Im γz_2)) (Legendre function of the second kind), G^m_s = G_s|T_m, and for f = Σc_f(m)q^m ∈ M^!_{−2j}, G_{1+j,f} = Σ_{m>0}c_f(−m)m^jG^m_{j+1}. Conjecture 1.1: if c_f(m) ∈ Z for m < 0 and (z_1, z_2) ∉ Z^j(f) = Σc_f(−m)m^jZ(m) with z_i of discriminant d_i, then (d_1d_2)^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(z_1, z_2) = (w_{d_1}w_{d_2}/4)log|α| for some α ∈ H_{d_1}H_{d_2}.

items.name: Theorem 1.2, Remark 1.3 and Corollary 1.4: partial averages and exponent-2 class groups
items.statement: Throughout require j∈Z_{>0} and f∈M!_{-2j} with integral principal part. For the individual-value corollary require avoidance of every contributing Hecke translate as in E5; distinct points do not suffice. Theorem 1.2: let j > 0, d_1 < 0 fundamental, d_2 < 0 with d_1d_2 not a square, C(d_1) = Σ_{Q∈𝒬_{d_1}/Γ}(2/w_Q)z_Q; put (k, H) = (Q(√d_1, √d_2), H_{d_2}(√d_1)) if j is odd and (Q(√d_2), H_{d_2}) if j is even. For every CM point z_2 of discriminant d_2 there are α ∈ H and r ∈ Z_{>0} with (d_1d_2)^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(C(d_1), z_2^σ) = r^{−1}log|α^σ| for all σ ∈ Gal(H/k); r depends only on d_2 (j even) or on d_1, d_2 (j odd) (Remark 1.3). Corollary 1.4: if d_1 < 0 is fundamental with class group trivial or of exponent 2, then (d_1d_2)^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(z_1, z_2) = r^{−1}log|α| with α ∈ H_{d_1}H_{d_2}, for all CM points z_1, z_2 of discriminants d_1, d_2 with (z_1, z_2) ∉ Z^j(f).

The intended endpoints are the small-CM formulas of Theorems 5.4/5.5 and Corollary 5.6 with integral coefficients and disjointness, the real-quadratic signed big-CM formula of Theorem 5.10, the off-Hecke-divisor same-field algebraicity of Theorem 6.1, the positive odd-weight higher Heegner height/modularity results of Theorems 6.5/6.12 with their fundamental-discriminant and coprimality hypotheses, and the positive-j partial averages/algebraicity of Section 7 after a complete normalization and integrality proof. /-- `ordinaryHypergeometric (a b c : 𝕂) : 𝔸 → 𝔸`, denoted `₂F₁`, is the ordinary hypergeometric map,

mathlib:Polynomial.shiftedLegendre.statement:
/-- `shiftedLegendre n` is an integer polynomial for each `n : ℕ`, defined by:
`Pₙ(x) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1)ᵏ * choose n k * choose (n + k) n * xᵏ`
These polynomials appear in combinatorics and the theory of orthogonal polynomials. -/
noncomputable def shiftedLegendre (n : ℕ) : ℤ[X] :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), C ((-1 : ℤ) ^ k * n.choose k * (n + k).choose n) * X ^ k

mathlib:Polynomial.factorial_mul_shifted.statement:
/-- The shifted Legendre polynomial multiplied by a factorial equals the higher-order derivative of
the combinatorial function `X ^ n * (1 - X) ^ n`. This is the analogue of Rodrigues' formula for
the shifted Legendre polynomials. -/
theorem factorial_mul_shiftedLegendre_eq (n : ℕ) : (n ! : ℤ[X]) * (shiftedLegendre n) =
    derivative^[n] (X ^ n * (1 - (X : ℤ[X])) ^ n) := by

mathlib:Polynomial.coeff_shiftedLegendre.statement:
/-- The coefficient of the shifted Legendre polynomial at `k` is
`(-1) ^ k * (n.choose k) * (n + k).choose n`. -/
theorem coeff_shiftedLegendre (n k : ℕ) :
    (shiftedLegendre n).coeff k = (-1) ^ k * n.choose k * (n + k).choose n := by
